Recent scholarship has, rightly, insisted on distinguishing between both the aims and originating theological contexts for the doctrines of the single operation and the single will, noting in particular that the latter was almost certainly not aimed at the miaphysite churches of the eastern provinces in the way that the doctrine of the single operation had been. Note that in a letter written in 634/635 in response to a patriarchal decision of August 633 to prohibit discussion of one or two operations, initially accepted by all the parties involved, Pope Honorius himself confessed a single will in Christ. Whether we should then conclude that the doctrine of the single will was an accidental outcome of imperial/patriarchal attempts to re-establish doctrinal order within the imperial church (see Jankowiak 2013c) remains moot: see esp. Tannous 2014: 31–32; 64–67; Allen 2009: 204–209. Monotheletism was the last in the series of Christological controversies over the nature of the Trinity and the relationship between its constituent elements. From the early fourth century the debate over the nature of Christ— divine, human, a mixture of both— had been carried on in the language of Greek philosophy, the chief dividing line evolving in the fifth century between those who believed that Christ was of two natures, human and divine, indivisible in a single divine essence (the “dyophysite” position that eventually became the orthodoxy of the imperial church), and those who thought that he was of one nature with the divinity (“miaphysite”), the creed that came to dominate in much of Syria, Egypt, and Armenia. The debate was carried on through a series of local and ecumenical church councils, and a first resolution was achieved at the Council of Chalcedon in 451 at which the dyophysite position prevailed (hence, “Chalcedonian”). But the debate rumbled on increasingly sharply through the later fifth and sixth centuries. See the summary of the theological issues in Hovorun 2015: 117–122; detailed analyses in Jankowiak 2009; Booth 2014; documents and texts: Winkelmann 2001; also Brandes 1998b; Uthemann 1997; Dagron 1993: 40–92; and the discussion in Chapter 2 of this volume.

The dating of the Bulgar campaign and the reason for Constantine IV’s absence during the council (lasting from the twelfth session, which began on March 22, 681, until the seventeenth session from September 11, 681) are disputed. There is no doubt that the emperor was absent for the sessions in question, and the generally-held view is that this was because he left to lead the expedition against the Bulgars. But in a carefully-argued and well-documented analysis of all the relevant sources De Gregorio and Kresten (2007) have argued, first that this expedition in fact took place in 680, and second, that the emperor’s absence in 681 was motivated by other internal political concerns, possibly in order to avoid dealing in person with the detailed condemnation of monotheletism (which would touch negatively upon past members of the imperial family, its supporters, and several former patriarchs of Constantinople), and to permit the emperor to adopt the role of neutral observer in the proceedings and their result. Jankowiak 2009: 474, note 136 dismisses this argument on the grounds that Theophanes’ text is not to be relied upon. In spite of this (generally accepted) comment on Theophanes’ text, the position adopted by De Gregorio and Kresten is persuasive. The issue awaits a final resolution.

In 565, the last year of the reign of Justinian I, the Eastern Roman Empire stretched from southern Spain and North Africa across to the Syrian desert and included Italy and Sicily, Sardinia and Corsica, the Balearic islands and the Balkans up to the Danube. Yet by 650 this picture had changed in ways that a century earlier would have been unimaginable. A glance at the map will help: on the one side, instead of the Sasanian Persian state, the enormous caliphate now dominates, stretching from the Atlantic to northern India and the central Asian steppe, and including the rich provinces of Syria, Iraq, and Egypt. On the other side, the little Eastern Roman Empire, after the collapse of Roman power following the Arab attacks and conquests of the years 634–650, reduced to a rump of its former self. By the year 700, all its Middle Eastern, North African, and western Mediterranean provinces had been lost, with the possible exception of a tenuous Roman presence in the Balearics into the second half of the eighth century and, of course, Sicily, southern Italy, and the exarchate of Ravenna in the north. The regions that remained were among the least wealthy of its former provinces, among which Egypt had contributed as the most productive, the main source of grain for Constantinople, and a major source of the state’s tax income. We get some idea of the enormity of the change when we look at the differences in income to the state from the middle of the sixth to the end of the seventh century.

While statistical comparisons are both difficult to make and problematic, it is certain that the Umayyad caliph in Damascus had, in theory at least, many times more resources available to him than had the Byzantine ruler in Constantinople— the income from Egypt and Syria alone probably amounted to more than three times the total revenue available to the eastern Roman emperor. (See Map 1.1.) Of course, this does not mean that it could all be thrown into war with the Byzantines—on the contrary, warfare in the northeast, in Transoxiana, and in North Africa or Spain; the costs of maintaining internal peace and political control; and the vast expenses entailed in maintaining the
dīwān

, the list of pensions owed to families associated with the Prophet’s original campaigns, were a substantial drain on caliphal income, and the devolved nature of both taxation and provincial government meant that the caliphs had a constant struggle on their hands to secure their share of the revenues from more distant provinces. Indeed, it has been noted that access to these resources, especially those from Egypt, would not have been straightforward, and was on occasion probably quite limited.

Nevertheless, the disparity was massive, and the investment both in large-scale expeditions as well as constant independent raids and attacks deep into east Roman lands throughout the period ca. 660–780 can be shown to have had a dramatic impact on economy and society. Both textual and, more importantly, paleo-environmental evidence can be adduced to demonstrate just how this affected the Byzantine landscape and Byzantine society.

在一份七世纪的记述中，被围困的堡垒城镇欧凯塔（Euchaïta，比这里考虑的地区偏北得多）的居民考虑放弃家园，以寻找一个不那么危险的环境（在一两个有记载的案例中确实发生了这样的事），而文本几乎机械地说"当萨拉森人每年的袭掠到来时"。

Apart from the archaeological and survey evidence for the shrinkage and fortification of many minor as well as larger urban settlements, along with a high degree of localization of exchange and commerce, the government at Constantinople undertook the compulsory transplanting of captive populations from the Balkans into devastated regions of Asia Minor in order to make good the loss of manpower through captivity and death.

By the middle of the eighth century, even Constantinople itself had to be repopulated, and for the first time in a century the major aqueduct bringing water into the city from outside was repaired and brought back into use.

There is also written and archaeological evidence for the flight of populations as well as the movement of settlements to more defensible locations, especially in the Aegean islands, the object of the attention of raids and attacks from the later seventh into the ninth and tenth centuries. Hagiographies of a slightly later period, the ninth, tenth, and eleventh centuries, all make reference to the devastation caused by such warfare; indeed, in some cases it seems that areas in Asia Minor first attacked in the seventh century, and regularly thereafter, were still only at the beginning of recovery in the later tenth century, a point nicely confirmed by palynological data for land use at this time, which I’ll discuss later. And this is, of course, apart from the narrative evidence of the chronicles and histories of the period.

In one seventh-century account, the population of the beleaguered fortress town of Euchaïta, much further north than the area under consideration here, considered abandoning their homes in an effort to locate a less hazardous environment (as did indeed happen in one or two documented cases), and the text speaks almost mechanically in terms of “when the yearly raid of the Saracens came.”

我只提一组例子来说明这个一般论点：拜占庭经济在边境地区及其后方受到这种持续战争的根本性影响；城市生活衰退；人口收缩；与伊斯兰邻邦相比，帝国深度贫困化。当然，我们也不应夸大——一些城镇受到的影响很小，存续了下来，显然乡村人口仍能继续生产足够的剩余，供政府提取资源。的确，重要的是要记住：第一，六世纪中叶大瘟疫之后，普遍的人口下降已经开始；第二，城市生活的变化速率也反映了既存的语境。因此，尽管某些地区城市聚落的数量在七、八世纪似乎经历了有时剧烈的减少，人口可能下降得不那么剧烈，乡村人口密度在某些地方可能反而增加，而城市"衰退"的速率反映了七世纪以前的语境——例如在相对城市化不足的地区不如在城市聚落水平高的地区那样明显。

I mention but one set of examples to illustrate the general point: that the Byzantine economy in the frontier districts and behind was radically affected by this constant warfare; that urbanism declined; that populations shrank; that the empire was, compared with its Islamic neighbor, deeply impoverished. Of course, neither should we exaggerate— some towns survived with minimal effects, and clearly the population of the countryside was able to continue producing enough surplus for the government to extract resources. Indeed, it is important to bear in mind that, first, a general demographic downturn had already set in after the great plague of the middle of the sixth century, but that, second, the rate of change in urbanism reflected also preexisting contexts. Thus, while the number of urban settlements in some regions appears to have undergone a sometimes drastic reduction in the seventh and eighth centuries, the population probably declined less dramatically, and rural population density may in places have increased, while the rate of urban “decline” reflected the pre-seventh-century context— less marked in relatively underurbanized districts than in those with a high level of urban settlement, for example.
史事梗概
The Story
为了提供一个结构或框架，以安置我将在以下各章处理的各种主题，并强调君士坦丁堡的统治者及其行政所面临挑战的戏剧性，值得非常简略地回顾一下从640年代到利奥三世统治时期（717–741）的事件进程。
近年来已有若干这样的综述，尽管一些问题仍有争议——无论在年代测定上，还是在不同且往往相互矛盾的记述之间的权衡上——但大多数写过这一时期的历史学家，无论其特定的切入角度如何，都认同总体图景。

In order to provide a structure or framework within which to locate the various topics I will address in the chapters that follow as well as to underline the dramatic nature of the challenges faced by rulers and their administration at Constantinople, it will be worth briefly reviewing, very summarily, the course of events from the 640s to the reign of Leo III (717–741).

There have been several such surveys in recent years, and while some issues remain contentious, either in respect of dating or in terms of the balance between different and often contradictory accounts, the general picture is agreed by most historians who have written on the period, whatever their particular angle of approach.
君士坦斯二世在641年11月9日成为唯一统治者时年仅十一岁。
他最初几年由元老院精英的资深成员主导，正如我们将在第4章所见，这一群体在七世纪影响力大增，肯定相比其在六世纪大部分时间里的角色与境遇而言。在这种情况下，发行一种设计截然不同、正面铸有"
en toutō nika
"（"凭此征服"［即十字架］）、背面铸有"
ananeōsis
"（"更新"）字样的铜币，发出了关于新政权意图的明确意识形态信息。
政治不确定性给了元老院机会，这可以从它在福卡斯、赫拉克洛纳斯与君士坦丁三世（希拉克略的长子）统治期间、以及君士坦斯二世最初几年里新的自信姿态看出。从他父亲的异母弟弟赫拉克洛纳斯及其继祖母玛尔提娜统治继承下来的政治困难——玛尔提娜曾任命亚美尼亚将军瓦伦提努斯为
警卫军
（excubitores，一支小型宫廷卫队）的
伯爵
（komēs）——继续是一个忧虑之源。
瓦伦提努斯据认为反映了宫廷与高级军方中一个更鹰派群体的利益，他已指挥一支驻扎在君士坦丁堡附近的庞大军队，似乎负责东部前线的作战。他是废黜玛尔提娜的关键推动者之一，并自立为共帝或凯撒（或试图如此）。但在试图通过他在都城的军队强加其意志时，引发了一场民众暴动，结果士兵被击败，他本人被私刑处死，很可能在644或645年。
Constans II was eleven years old when he became sole ruler on November 9, 641.

His first years were dominated by senior members of the senatorial elite, a group that, as we will see in Chapter 4, experienced a substantial increase in influence in the seventh century, certainly in comparison with its role and fortunes through much of the sixth century. In the circumstances, the issue of a copper coin with a radically different design and bearing the words “
en toutōnika
” (“conquer in this” [i.e., the cross]) on the obverse and “
ananeōsis
” (“renewal”) on the reverse sent a clear ideological message about the intentions of the new regime.

Political uncertainty offered the senate opportunities, something that can be seen from its new assertiveness during the reigns of Phocas and of Heraklonas and Constantine III (Heraclius’s eldest son) as well as during the first years of Constans II. The political difficulties inherited from the reign of his half-uncle Heraklonas and his step-grandmother, Martina, who had made the Armenian general Valentinus
komēs
of the
excubitores
(a small palatine guards unit), continued to be a source of concern.

Valentinus, who, it has been suggested, reflected the interests of a more hawkish group at court and in the senior military, already commanded a substantial army based near Constantinople and seems to have been in charge of operations on the eastern front. He was one of the key movers in deposing Martina and had himself proclaimed co-emperor or Caesar (or tried to do so). But in attempting to impose his will through his troops in the capital, a popular riot was set in motion, which resulted in the defeat of the soldiers and his own lynching, probably in 644 or 645.

帝国的外部处境危殆。玛尔提娜倾向于在可能时与阿拉伯人和平谈判，结果按照牧首居鲁士达成的一项协议，拜占庭军队于642年9月撤出亚历山大里亚。阿拉伯领袖阿慕尔·本·阿斯（ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs）于9月29日进城。随后伊斯兰权力沿北非沿海行省缓慢扩张——先是五城地区（Pentapolis），然后643年是对的黎波里（Tripolis）。645年拜占庭曾短暂重新占领亚历山大里亚，当时阿慕尔被召回麦加，但帝国军队于646年被永久驱逐。从640年代初起，阿拉伯军队也开始袭掠安纳托利亚与亚美尼亚，尽管在亚美尼亚军队统帅、最重要的亚美尼亚亲王之一狄奥多尔·勒什图尼（Theodore Rštuni）麾下取得了一些罗马人的胜利，但也有一些重大失败，尤其642/643年在罗马将军普罗科皮乌斯麾下。647年穆阿维叶袭掠卡帕多西亚，围攻凯撒利亚，袭掠弗里吉亚，并进攻阿莫里翁。没有建立永久基地，但大量战利品被带回大马士革。在此之前，拜占庭对海洋的控制一直未受挑战，例如重新占领亚历山大里亚就证明了这一点；但阿拉伯领导层很快意识到需要海军存在，以应对并先发制人地阻止拜占庭对沿海地区尤其叙利亚的攻击，并扩展其征服。穆阿维叶似乎是第一个对此采取行动的人。649年发生了第一次阿拉伯海军远征，目标是塞浦路斯。该岛首府君士坦提亚（Constantia）被强攻夺取。650年发生第二次攻击，开始时得到增援的守军干脆放弃该岛撤退。两次袭掠都缴获大量战利品和数以万计的俘虏。无论这些攻击是否意在牵制，阿拉伯舰队随后围攻了叙利亚沿海阿拉杜斯岛（Aradus，即阿尔瓦德，Arwad）上的帝国基地。由于没有明确的解围希望，守军达成协议投降。另一次对小亚细亚的袭掠目标是伊苏里亚行省，作为回应，双方商定了为期三年的休战。

The external situation of the empire was precarious. Martina had favored peaceful negotiations with the Arabs where possible, and as a result and in accordance with an agreement reached by the patriarch Cyrus, Byzantine troops evacuated Alexandria in September 642. The Arab leader ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs entered the city on September 29. There then followed a slow expansion of Islamic power along the coastal provinces of North Africa— the Pentapolis, then in 643 Tripolis. A temporary Byzantine reoccupation of Alexandria took place in 645, when ʿAmr was called back to Mecca, but the imperial forces were expelled permanently in 646. From the early 640s, Arab forces started raiding Anatolia and Armenia as well, and although some Roman successes were registered under the commander of the forces in Armenia, Theodore Rštuni, one of the foremost Armenian princes, there were also some major defeats, notably in the year 642/643 under the Roman general Procopius. In 647 Muʿāwiya raided Cappadocia, besieged Caesarea, raided into Phrygia, and attacked Amorium. No permanent bases were established, but an enormous booty was taken back to Damascus. Until this point Byzantine control of the sea had been unchallenged, as the reoccupation of Alexandria, for example, demonstrated, but the Arab leadership soon grasped the need for naval presence in order to meet and preempt Byzantine attacks on coastal regions, especially in Syria, as well as to extend their conquests. Muʿāwiya seems to have been the first to act on this. In 649 the first Arab naval expedition took place, directed against Cyprus. Constantia, the island’s capital, was taken by storm. A second attack took place in 650, at the outset of which the reinforced defenders simply abandoned the island and withdrew. Both raids netted a large booty and tens of thousands of captives. Whether these attacks were intended as diversions or not, the Arab fleet then laid siege to the imperial base on the island of Aradus (Arwad) off the Syrian coast. With no clear hope of relief, the garrison came to terms and surrendered. Another raid into Asia Minor targeted the province of Isauria, and in response a truce was agreed for three years.

648或649年，帝国政府颁布法令，规定亚美尼亚教会应服从君士坦丁堡教座与卡尔西顿信经。在649年召开的德温（Dvin）宗教会议上，亚美尼亚教士与若干亲王——包括拜占庭总督狄奥多尔·勒什图尼——拒绝并谴责了帝国法令。与此同时，653年，随着650年在该地区商定的罗马—阿拉伯休战破裂，狄奥多尔转而效忠阿拉伯人，这一举动导致一支庞大的罗马军队在幼发拉底河被击败，至少部分是由于狄奥多尔之子瓦尔德（Vard）的背叛——他指挥的一支亚美尼亚分遣队在交战期间倒向阿拉伯人。这迫使君士坦斯集结军队东征以应对局势。该地区大多数亚美尼亚与帝国军队抛弃了狄奥多尔。尽管这次远征就其所能及而言是成功的，穆阿维叶与此同时却在准备一次意义大得多的行动，这次直指君士坦丁堡本身，他于653年发动，从而迫使君士坦斯返回保卫都城，亚美尼亚局势随之恢复原状。皇帝还面临一场涉及元老院成员与亚美尼亚军事贵族的阴谋，其中一些人在当时驻色雷斯的军队中担任指挥。尽管阴谋被人告发、皇帝得以逮捕阴谋者，但它可能既反映了元老院对这位如今开始摆脱此前主导他的顾问、申明独立的皇帝的敌意，也反映了亚美尼亚精英中更普遍的不满——他们后来也被证明难以驾驭，并可能最终成为他倒台的关键角色。君士坦斯留下将军马里亚努斯（Marianus）负责东部，但他随后被一支亚美尼亚叛军与阿拉伯援军的联合部队击败。亚美尼亚一直处于穆斯林统治之下，直到656年哈里发奥斯曼（ʿUthmān）被谋杀，亲王哈马扎斯普·马米科尼扬（Hamazasp Mamikonian）重新回到拜占庭阵营。

In 648 or 649 the imperial government had decreed that the Armenian Church should be subordinate to the see of Constantinople and the Chalcedonian creed. At the synod of Dvin, held in 649, the Armenian clergy and a number of princes, including the Byzantine governor, Theodore Rštuni, rejected and condemned the imperial decree. Meanwhile, in 653 and following the breakdown of a Roman-Arab truce in the region agreed in 650, Theodore transferred his allegiance to the Arabs, a move that led to the defeat of a substantial Roman force on the Euphrates, brought about in part at least by the betrayal of the Roman troops by Theodore’s son, Vard, who commanded an Armenian contingent that went over to the Arabs during the engagement. This forced Constans to assemble his forces and march east to deal with the situation. Most of the Armenian and imperial forces in the region abandoned Theodore. Although the expedition was successful, as far as it went, Muʿāwiya was meanwhile preparing a much more significant move, this time against Constantinople itself, which he launched in 653, thus compelling Constans’s return to defend the capital, upon which the Armenian situation reverted to its former state. The emperor was also faced with a plot involving members of the senate and of the Armenian military aristocracy, some of whom held commands in the forces then in Thrace. While the plot was betrayed and the emperor was able to arrest the conspirators, it may represent both senatorial hostility to the emperor who was now beginning to assert his independence from the advisors who had hitherto dominated as well as a more general discontent among the Armenian elite, who were later also to prove difficult and who may eventually have been key players in his downfall. Constans left the general Marianus in charge in the east, but he was subsequently defeated by a combined force of Armenian rebels with Arab reinforcements. Armenia remained under Muslim domination until the murder of the caliph ʿUthmān in 656, when the prince Hamazasp Mamikonian returned to the Byzantine fold.

阿拉伯海军建造迅速推进，如前所述，653年休战结束时敌对行动恢复。作为对都城大规模进攻的准备，654年罗得岛遭攻击并被蹂躏（倒塌的巨像被卖给一位埃德萨商人），科斯岛被夺取，克里特遭劫掠。655年，君士坦斯亲自指挥帝国舰队，在吕基亚沿海与阿拉伯军队海上交锋，但遭惨败，仅以身免。对君士坦丁堡的进攻现在加速。另一支舰队从埃及出发，伴随运输船，同时两支庞大军队已开进安纳托利亚，一支654年在卡帕多西亚建立基地，另一支由穆阿维叶亲自指挥，穿越高原直抵博斯普鲁斯海峡。但在一场给阿拉伯舰队造成重大损失的风暴的帮助下，罗马海军力量重新确立，进攻被击败。没有足够的海军支援，陆军无能为力，被撤回。卡帕多西亚的部队也被击败并逐出罗马领土，罗马野战军再次活跃于亚美尼亚。

Arab naval construction had proceeded apace and, as noted, hostilities resumed at the end of the truce in 653. Preparatory to the major attack against the capital, Rhodes was attacked and ravaged in 654 (the fallen Colossus was sold off to an Edessan merchant), Cos was taken, and Crete was pillaged. In 655, taking personal command of the imperial fleet, Constans confronted the Arab forces at sea off the coast of Lycia but was crushingly defeated and barely escaped with his life. The campaign against Constantinople now picked up pace. Another fleet sailed from Egypt accompanying transport vessels, while two substantial forces had marched into Anatolia, one establishing a base in Cappadocia in 654, and the other, under Muʿāwiya’s personal command, marching across the plateau to the Bosphorus Strait. But aided by a storm that inflicted substantial damage on the Arab fleet, Roman naval power was reasserted and the attack defeated. Without adequate naval support, the land forces could do nothing and were withdrawn. The Cappadocian force was also defeated and driven out of Roman territory, and Roman field forces were again active in Armenia.
这些失败，加上高加索与呼罗珊的若干其他挫折与叛乱，以及对哈里发奥斯曼领导的不满，导致麦加的争端与656年哈里发被谋杀。由此产生的内乱（
菲特纳
，fitna）——一方希望通过辩论由会议选出哈里发，另一方相信领导权应留在先知家族内——首先导致阿里（ʿAli）被宣布为哈里发，然后导致全面内战。现在展开的冲突为帝国提供了重要的喘息之机，因为为了集中力量击败阿里及其支持者，穆阿维叶于659年同意休战，休战持续到661/662年他最终胜利。
659年秋，君士坦斯再次进军亚美尼亚，以巩固他通过向亚美尼亚及更广泛的高加索精英赠送礼物、头衔与其他帝国恩赏而在东部前线建立起来的附庸亲王体系。其中包括高加索阿尔巴尼亚亲王朱安舍尔（Juansher），但在君士坦斯离开后一年内，朱安舍尔与该地区大多数其他领主已重新效忠穆阿维叶。
在安纳托利亚，从662/663年起对堡垒与聚落的袭掠与攻击持续不断；的确，随着穆阿维叶积累资源、再次削弱拜占庭在安纳托利亚的抵抗，作为对君士坦丁堡第二次大规模进攻的前奏，攻击的强度增加了。

These defeats, combined with a number of other setbacks and rebellions in the Caucasus and in Khorasan, as well as discontent about the leadership of the caliph ʿUthmān, led to disputes in Mecca and the murder of the caliph in 656. The resulting civil strife (
fitna

) between those who wanted a caliph chosen by council through debate and those who believed leadership should stay within the Prophet’s family led, first, to the proclamation of ʿAli as caliph and then to outright civil war. The conflict that now developed offered an important breathing space for the empire, since in order to focus on defeating ʿAli and his supporters Muʿāwiya agreed to a truce in 659, which lasted until 661/662 and his final victory.

In the fall of 659 Constans had again marched to Armenia in order to bolster the system of client princes on the eastern front that he had been building up through gifts, titles, and other imperial endowments to the Armenian and Caucasian elites more broadly. Among these were Juansher, prince of Caucasian Albania, but within a year of Constans’s departure Juansher and most of the other lords of the region had returned to their allegiance to Muʿāwiya.

In Anatolia, raids and attacks on fortresses and settlements continued from 662/663; indeed, the intensity of the attacks increased as Muʿāwiya built up his resources and softened up Byzantine resistance in Anatolia once again as a preliminary to a second major attack on Constantinople.

但战争的短暂停顿有重要后果，因为它使君士坦斯得以把注意力转向巴尔干。在这里帝国军队几乎一直处于防御。658年，当哈里发国的内战减轻了对安纳托利亚的压力时，君士坦斯发动了对Sklaviniai（斯拉夫人地区）的远征，据报他击败了许多部落并抓获许多俘虏。数千名俘虏及其家属被重新安置到安纳托利亚遭受破坏或荒废的地区，而一些俘虏可能被编入行省军队为兵——这一政策为后来的皇帝包括君士坦丁四世与查士丁尼二世所沿用。有人主张正是在此时君士坦斯及其顾问重组了帝国防御与军队，创造了后来史料所称的
军区
（themata），即军事行省。这里只需说，没有丝毫证据支持这种想法，尽管军队确实被重新分配到安纳托利亚各行省，这些变化很可能有行政后果。我们将在第7章回到这个问题。

But the short pause in the warfare had important consequence, since it permitted Constans to turn his attention to the Balkans. Here imperial troops had been more or less constantly on the defensive. In 658, while civil war in the caliphate relieved the pressure on Anatolia, Constans launched an expedition into the Sklaviniai, the regions of the Slavs, where he reportedly defeated many tribes and took many prisoners. Several thousands of prisoners with their families were resettled in devastated or deserted areas of Anatolia, while some of the prisoners were probably enrolled as soldiers in the provincial armies— a policy that was pursued by later emperors including both Constantine IV and Justinian II. Some have argued that it was at this time that Constans and his advisors reorganized imperial defenses and the armies, creating what the later sources refer to as
themata

, or military provinces. Suffice to say here that there is not a shred of evidence to support such an idea, although the armies were certainly redistributed across the Anatolian provinces and there were likely administrative consequences of these changes. We will return to this question in Chapter 7.

君士坦斯的统治被从希拉克略继承的、与一能论和一志论教义相关的问题所困扰，我将在第2、4章更详细地考察其中一些问题。早在第一次阿拉伯攻击之前的几年，希拉克略与牧首塞尔吉乌斯（Sergius）就已努力寻找一个能促进一性论派与二性论派共同体重新统一的方案。一能论是关于基督"单一能量"或"单一行动"的教义。它在620年代后期于君士坦丁堡精心构建，它所处理的问题已在某些教会圈子里讨论了几十年，而塞尔吉乌斯所呈现的成熟教义绝非绝对的新事物。但在620与630年代，它有了额外的价值：提供了一个调和一性论派与二性论派教会的机会，很可能是怀着这一目的被引入作为帝国教会的官方立场。它起初受到东方教会的一些人士的好评，并构成此后不久亚美尼亚与迦勒底教会接受与君士坦丁堡共融的基础。
尽管亚历山大里亚牧首也接受了它，教皇霍诺里乌斯（Honorius）亦然（尽管有自己的保留），东部行省还有若干其他人接受，但耶路撒冷牧首索弗罗尼乌斯（Sophronius）未被说服，正是他的反对部分导致不久后对这一教义的重新思考。
关于大叙利亚各行省对这一拒绝帝国赞助之神学的反应，我们没有信息，只知道显然索弗罗尼乌斯并非孤身一人，几年后构成反对核心的包括修道院院长忏悔者马克西姆（即便似乎也很清楚，马克西姆花了一些时间才澄清自己在这个问题上的想法）。
鉴于后来在阿非利加的发展（我们将看到），并非不可能的是，在叙利亚行省，这场关于教义的冲突损害了许多理解该问题的人支持帝国政策抵抗入侵者的意愿。

Constans’s reign was dogged by problems inherited from Heraclius associated with the doctrines of monoenergism and monotheletism, and I will look in more detail at some of these issues in Chapters 2 and 4. Already in the years preceding the first Arab attacks Heraclius and the patriarch Sergius had struggled to find a formula that would facilitate the reunification of the miaphysite and dyophysite communities. Monoenergism was the doctrine of the “single energy” or “operation” of Christ. Elaborated at Constantinople during the later 620s, the issues it addressed had been under discussion in some ecclesiastical circles for several decades and a developed doctrine, as presented by Sergius, was by no means an absolute novelty. But in the 620s and 630s it had the added value of presenting an opportunity to reconcile the miaphysite and dyophysite churches, and was probably introduced as the official position of the imperial church with this in mind. It was at first well received by some elements of the eastern churches and formed the basis upon which the Armenian and Chaldean churches accepted communion with Constantinople shortly thereafter.

Although the patriarch of Alexandria also accepted it, as did the pope, Honorius (although with his own reservations), along with a number of others in the eastern provinces, the patriarch Sophronius of Jerusalem was not persuaded, and it was in part his opposition that led after a short time to the rethinking of the doctrine.

We have no information about the response of the provinces of Greater Syria to this rejection of an imperially sponsored theology except that it is clear that Sophronius was not alone, and that among those who formed the heart of the opposition a few years later was the abbot Maximus the Confessor (even if it also seems clear that Maximus took some time to clarify his own thinking on the subject).

In light of later developments in Africa, as we shall see, it is not impossible that in the Syrian provinces this conflict over dogma damaged the willingness of many of those who understood the issue to support imperial policy in resisting the invader.
为回应索弗罗尼乌斯等人的反对，并继636年在塞浦路斯召开的一次会议之后——塞尔吉乌斯、其亲密盟友亚历山大里亚的居鲁士以及索弗罗尼乌斯都出席了那次会议——希拉克略于636或638年（年代有争议）颁布了所谓的
《信仰阐述》
（Ekthesis），尽管这份文件的文本很可能是牧首塞尔吉乌斯的手笔。讨论"行动"问题被禁止，同时试图围绕基督单一意志的概念达成进一步妥协，该意志超越其人性与神性两者。尽管这种"一志论"路径显然意在平息新卡尔西顿教会内部的讨论与异议，并使局势恢复到索弗罗尼乌斯反对之前的常态，但
《信仰阐述》
却产生了相反的效果——的确，似乎正是这份文件激起了舆论并最终导致叛乱。虽然它不太可能以维持东部行省一性论派共同体的忠诚为特定目标，但这仍是政府的核心关切，因为在此阶段人们假定帝国终将在某个时候击败入侵者并恢复对该地区的控制。
耶路撒冷牧首区似乎处于反对的核心，但随着修士与教士从巴勒斯坦西迁、远离伊斯兰对其行省的新统治，他们把对帝国立场的敌意也带了过来。
忏悔者马克西姆成为这些流徙者中的突出人物，他拥有广泛的通信网络，包括高级教士与修士，以及国家军政两界的要员。他可能也与希拉克略本人家族有联系，这一联系是在618–628年波斯占领巴勒斯坦期间他逗留阿非利加时建立的。

In response to the opposition from Sophronius and others, and following on from a council held on Cyprus in 636 at which Sergius, his close ally Cyrus of Alexandria, as well as Sophronius were all present, Heraclius had issued the so-called
Ekthesis

in 636 or 638 (the date is contested), although the text of this document was likely the work of the patriarch Sergius. Discussion of the issue of operations was prohibited, and at the same time a further compromise was attempted based around the concept of a single will of Christ, transcending both his human and divine natures. While this “monothelete” approach was clearly intended to silence discussion and dissent within the neo-Chalcedonian church as well as to normalize the situation as it had been before Sophronius’s opposition, the
Ekthesis

had the opposite effect— indeed, it appears that it was this document that inflamed opinion and ultimately led to rebellion. And while it was unlikely to have had the specific aim of maintaining the loyalty of the miaphysite communities in the eastern provinces, this was still a central concern of the government, since at this stage it was assumed that the empire would at some point defeat the invader and recover its control in the region.

The patriarchate of Jerusalem seems to have been at the heart of opposition, but as monks and clergy from Palestine moved westward and away from the new Islamic domination of their province, they brought their hostility to the imperial position with them.

Maximus the Confessor became a prominent figure among these migrants, a man with a widespread network of correspondents, including senior churchmen and monastics as well as leading officials of the state, both military and civilian. It is possible that he also had a connection with the family of Heraclius himself, a connection made during a stay in Africa during the Persian occupation of Palestine in the period 618–628.

但随着对帝国政策的反对在西方增长，在北叙利亚与巴勒斯坦，后来的证据表明，在某个时候——肯定从681–682年会议（见下）之时起——新卡尔西顿共同体不顾索弗罗尼乌斯的立场，带着某种热情拥护一志论方案。同样的情况可能也确实适用于安纳托利亚剩余帝国领土的大部分地区，这一事实本身可能是说服君士坦斯及其顾问维持该政策作为官方路线的一个重要因素。它肯定意味着单一意志教义不仅仅是帝国政治的权术或工具，而是在更广泛的社会中、至少在某些地区有真正的根基。

与此同时，在北非，646年最初几个月里召开了若干地方宗教会议，很可能是马克西姆反对一志论运动的结果。结果是对帝国宗教政策的谴责。被流放的君士坦丁堡一志论牧首皮鲁斯（Pyrrhus）在一场公开辩论中输给马克西姆，辩论由总督（军事长官）格里高利（Gregory）本人主持；很可能正是北非主教们反对帝国政策的团结，鼓励了总督于646/647年宣布反对君士坦斯的统治并自立为帝。他短暂的篡夺以失败告终：次年在苏费图拉（Sufetula）附近与阿拉伯袭掠者作战时格里高利被杀，此后似乎安排了休战。袭掠者撤退后，帝国权威迅速重新确立，以迦太基铸币厂特别发行银币为标志。为重新申明帝国权威，牧首保罗（Paul）于648年以君士坦斯的名义颁布另一道法令，即所谓的
《信仰规范》
（Typos）。它命令将
《信仰阐述》
从圣索菲亚大教堂的前厅移除，但不允许进一步讨论。基督单一意志或单一行动的问题不得辩论。但这不太可能产生一致，而在649年于罗马召开的拉特兰会议上，在新当选的教皇马丁（Martin）主持下，出席的105位西方主教谴责了
《信仰阐述》
与
《信仰规范》
，连同牧首塞尔吉乌斯、皮鲁斯以及当时在任的保罗。
会议决议在东西方教座传阅，副本送往君士坦丁堡。无论教皇在给皇帝的信中措辞多么礼貌，对帝国权威的挑战都不可能被误解：

But while opposition to imperial policy grew in the west, in North Syria and Palestine later evidence would suggest that at some point, and certainly from the time of the council of 681–682 (see below) the neo-Chalcedonian communities espoused the formula of monotheletism with some enthusiasm in spite of Sophronius’s position. The same may indeed also have been true of much of the remaining imperial territory in Anatolia, and this fact in itself may have been a significant factor in persuading Constans and his advisors to maintain the policy as the official line. It certainly implies that the doctrine of the single will was not merely an artifice or tool of imperial politics but had a genuine hold in society more broadly, at least in certain regions.

Meanwhile, in North Africa several local synods took place across the first months of 646, most likely a result of Maximus’s campaign against monotheletism. The result was a condemnation of imperial religious policy. The exiled monothelete patriarch of Constantinople, Pyrrhus, lost a public debate with Maximus, presided over by the exarch (military governor) himself, Gregory; and it was probably the solidarity of the North African bishops in opposing imperial policy that encouraged the exarch to declare his opposition to Constans’s rule in 646/647 and have himself proclaimed emperor. His short-lived usurpation met with failure when in the following year Gregory was killed fighting Arab raiders near Sufetula, after which a truce seems to have been arranged. When the raiders withdrew, imperial authority was rapidly reestablished, marked by a special issue of silver by the mint at Carthage. In an effort to reassert imperial authority, the patriarch Paul issued another decree in Constans’s name, the so-called
Typos,
in 648. This ordered that the
Ekthesis

be removed from the narthex of Hagia Sophia, but no further discussion was to be permitted. The issue of a single will or operation of Christ was not to be debated. But this was unlikely to produce agreement, and at the Lateran council held in Rome in 649, under the newly elected Pope Martin, the 105 western bishops who were present condemned both
Ekthesis
and
Typos,
together with the patriarchs Sergius and Pyrrhus as well as the then incumbent Paul.

The decisions of the synod were circulated in both eastern and western sees and copies sent to Constantinople. However politely the pope may have expressed himself in his letter to the emperor, the challenge to imperial authority could not be mistaken:

致最虔诚、最安详的主上与凯旋的胜利者、［我们的］爱上帝与我们主耶稣基督之子君士坦丁奥古斯都，来自众仆之仆、主教马丁……我们特此告知您虔诚而安详的权威：我们所有人聚集在您这座爱基督、侍奉上帝的罗马城……已以宗教会议的方式确认正统信仰的虔诚定义，并恰当地废除异端分子——无论过去还是现在［包括君士坦丁堡牧首塞尔吉乌斯、皮鲁斯与保罗］——不和谐的教义，他们因其推理的乖谬而自绝于真理。他们胆敢以谗言蒙蔽陛下，也曾用同样的手段蒙蔽陛下受祝福的先祖父［希拉克略］，以便罪恶地把他们自己的罪责强加于他人……因为不仅虔诚的会众因而震惊，如今连无神的蛮族也在嘲笑我们信仰的伟大奥秘……因此，为了向您的权威清楚表明两者之间的区别——即虔诚的教父及其定义，与不敬的人及其教义——我们……已寄上我们的会议记录，连同其希腊语译文，恳求并劝勉在上帝之事上智慧的陛下，屈尊予以恰当的阅读，并以虔诚的法律谴责上述异端分子及其异端……因为当陛下在主里拥有正确的信仰时，主武装他的造物以抵御敌人，他必将理所当然地援助您的权威去征服您的敌人。

To the most pious and serene master and triumphant victor, [our] son who loves God and our Lord Jesus Christ, Constantine Augustus, from bishop Martin, servant of the servants of God. . . We therefore inform your pious and serene authority that, assembling together in this your Christ-loving and God-serving city of Rome, all of us. . . have confirmed synodically the pious definition of the orthodox faith, and fitly annulled the discordant teachings of the heretics, both past and present [including the patriarchs of Constantinople Sergius, Pyrrhus and Paul] who in the perversity of their reasoning separated themselves from the truth. They lawlessly seduced the ears of your serenity, as also those of your serenity’s blessed grandfather of blessed memory [Heraclius], so that they might criminally inflict their own guilt on others. . . For not only have the pious congregations been scandalized, but the godless barbarians are now mocking the great mystery of our confession. . . In order, therefore, to show clearly to your authority the difference between the two— that is, the fathers of piety and their definitions, and the impious men and their doctrines— we. . . have sent our synodical proceedings, together with their translation into the Greek language, beseeching and exhorting your serenity, wise in the things of God, to deign to give them a fitting reading, and to condemn by laws of piety the said heretics together with their heresy. . . For when your serenity has a correct faith in the Lord, who arms his creation to ward off the enemy, he will deservedly give aid to your authority in conquering your enemies.
近期研究已清楚表明，会议本身由马克西姆及其盟友策划和主导，旨在取得尽可能大的宣传效果。
Recent research has made it clear that the council itself was orchestrated and dominated by Maximus and his allies and aimed at achieving the greatest possible propaganda effect.
这样的回应——对帝国政策的公开纠正——不可能被忽视。在这种对帝国政策的拒绝中，攸关的是君士坦斯本人的正统性以及他是否有资格登上皇位。政府命令拉文纳总督奥林皮乌斯（Olympius）逮捕马丁，并强迫西方主教确认
《信仰规范》
。然而像阿非利加的格里高利一样，奥林皮乌斯似乎觉得反叛并自立为帝更可以接受。鉴于政府在东部面临的困难（对塞浦路斯的攻击以及对君士坦丁堡本身日益增长的威胁），政府无能为力。奥林皮乌斯是否最终打算进军君士坦丁堡本身（如有人推测），仍不得而知，因为史料没有提及。他起初似乎意在夺取西西里，是因为它当时是一次重大阿拉伯袭掠的目标，还是因为它的财富，或两者兼有，同样不得而知。

无论哪种情况，他的独立都是短暂的，因为他652年死于感染，到653年6月新总督已掌权并得以逮捕教皇。马丁于12月抵达君士坦丁堡。对他的审判完全基于针对他的政治指控——包括支持奥林皮乌斯的篡夺——进行，他不出所料被判有罪。起初被判死刑，很快减为流放克里米亚的赫尔松（Cherson）。他656年去世。对马克西姆的审判与审讯并无不同——他被控叛国与出卖帝国，在帝国当局眼中这完全正当，尽管显然政府花了很大力气试图说服他与帝国教会共融、并承认皇帝的权威是绝对的。在662年于君士坦丁堡召集的一次宗教会议上，审判与审讯的结果得到确认。马克西姆被处以残刑，662年死于高加索拉齐卡（Lazica）的斯赫马里翁（Schemarion）堡垒的流放中。政府对从帝国观点看只能、而且完全正当地被理解为叛国之事的回应，在当时语境下完全可以预料。

Such a response, a public corrective to imperial policy, could not be ignored. At issue in such a rejection of imperial policy was the orthodoxy and fitness to sit on the imperial throne of Constans himself. The government ordered Olympius, the exarch of Ravenna, to arrest Martin and to compel western episcopal confirmation of the
Typos.

Like Gregory in Africa, however, Olympius seems to have found it more acceptable to rebel and to have himself proclaimed emperor. The government could do nothing in light of the difficulties it faced in the east (attacks against Cyprus and a growing threat to Constantinople itself). Whether Olympius intended eventually to move on Constantinople itself, as some have suggested, remains unknown since the sources make no reference to this. He initially seems to have aimed to seize Sicily, whether because it was at that point the target of a major Arab raid or because of its wealth, or both, is again unknown.

In either case, his independence was short-lived since he died of an infection in 652, and by June 653 the new exarch was in command and had been able to arrest the pope. Martin arrived in Constantinople in December. His trial was conducted entirely on the basis of the political case against him, including supporting the usurpation of Olympius, and he was predictably enough found guilty. Initially sentenced to death, this was quickly commuted to exile in Cherson in the Crimea. He died in 656. The trial and interrogations of Maximus went no differently—he was accused, quite justifiably in the eyes of the imperial authorities, of high treason and the betrayal of the empire, although it is clear that the government invested much effort in trying to persuade him to take communion with the imperial church and recognize that the emperor’s authority was absolute. At a synod convened at Constantinople in 662 the results of the trial and interrogations were confirmed. Maximus was punished by mutilation and died in exile in 662 in the fortress of Schemarion in Lazica, in the Caucasus. The government response to what, from the imperial point of view, could only, and quite legitimately be understood as treason was in the context entirely predictable.

body.review: 原书此处（第39页）记教皇马丁卒于656年，第40页则作655年，两处各依原印。

children: 正如我们可能预料的，尽管君士坦丁堡教座连同安条克教座顺从帝国政策，罗马方面仍然抵制帝国政策；然而教士们确实接受了君士坦丁堡强加的新教皇尤金尼乌斯（Eugenius）。655年马丁在流放中去世前不久也承认了他，从而使帝国政府得以在马克西姆受审时告知他整个教会已团结一致、如今只有他一人不合拍（尽管关于马克西姆审判性质的报告已从君士坦丁堡先到撒丁、再到罗马。面对民众的愤怒，尤金尼乌斯被迫拒绝新牧首彼得（Peter）的会议书信）。
尽管马克西姆不愿屈服于这种压力，政府因此得以推行其政策，抵抗似乎非常有限。
但整个漫长拖延的事件引发了一大堆关于帝国权威、关于信仰、教义与世俗帝国及其统治者之间关系的问题。皇帝的角色及其作为上帝代理者的职能被置于审视之下，而君士坦丁堡政权坚持必须推行帝国一志论，反映了它自身对帝国权威的焦虑。也许确实，到640年代，一志论意欲争取的一性论派民众所居住的许多地区已不再由帝国控制，但有充分理由相信政府假定它们的丧失是暂时的、可以逆转，至少直到680年代如此。

As we might expect, while the see of Constantinople, along with that of Antioch, conformed to imperial policy, Roman sentiment remained hostile; however, the clergy did accept the new pope, Eugenius, imposed by Constantinople. Shortly before his death in exile in 655, Martin also recognized him, thus permitting the imperial government to inform Maximus during his own trial that the whole church was united and that he alone was now out of step (although reports from Constantinople had reached first Sardinia and then Rome about the nature of Maximus’ trial. In the face of popular anger, Eugenius was forced to reject the synodical letters of the new patriarch, Peter).
And although Maximus would not give in to this pressure, the government was thus able to enforce its policy, and resistance seems to have been very limited.

But the whole long, drawn-out episode raised a host of questions about imperial authority and about the relationship between belief, dogma, and the secular empire and its rulers. The emperor’s role and his function as God’s vicegerent had been placed under scrutiny, while the insistence of the Constantinopolitan regime that imperial monotheletism must be enforced reflected its own anxieties about the imperial authority. It may be true that many of the lands at whose miaphysite populations monotheletism had been aimed were by the 640s lost to the empire, but there is good reason to believe that the government assumed that their loss was temporary and could be reversed, at least until the 680s.

宫廷与高级军官中显然对帝国政策有些疑虑。君士坦斯的兄弟狄奥多西（Theodosius）可能卷入了一场反一志论群体废黜君士坦斯的阴谋，尽管证据不清楚。但654年君士坦斯加冕其子君士坦丁为共帝，659年他的两个较年幼的儿子希拉克略与提比略也也获加冕为帝。通过这样越过其弟狄奥多西，君士坦斯显然意在完全排除他，660年狄奥多西被剃度出家，实际上被排除在帝位继承之外，不久后他被谋杀。662年君士坦丁堡谴责并流放忏悔者马克西姆的宗教会议，很可能与狄奥多西的阴谋及其处决有关。尽管这些事件在君士坦丁堡引起相当不安，但威胁不可能太明显或太严重，否则皇帝不会离开都城。

There was clearly some doubt at court and among senior military officers about imperial policy. Constans’s brother Theodosius may have been involved in a plot of antimonothelete groups to depose Constans, although the evidence is not clear. But in 654 Constans crowned his son Constantine co-emperor and in 659 his two younger sons, Heraclius and Tiberius, were also raised to the imperial dignity. In thus passing over his younger brother Theodosius, Constans clearly aimed to exclude him altogether, and in 660 Theodosius was tonsured, effectively excluding him from the imperial succession, and shortly thereafter he was murdered. The synod of 662 in Constantinople at which Maximus the Confessor was condemned and exiled is very likely connected with Theodosius’ plot and his execution. Although these events caused considerable disquiet in Constantinople, the threat cannot have been too obvious or serious, for otherwise the emperor would not have left the capital.

继662年一志论宗教会议之后，君士坦斯出发进行一次重大的西征，这一举动更可能反映与粮食供给及西西里、北非其他资源相关的关切，而非对他明显不得人心的回应。君士坦斯很可能把西部行省视为帝国存续在战略与政治上的关键，因为尽管有伊斯兰的海军挑战，帝国仍由地中海联结在一起。风险相当大，尤其就安纳托利亚而言，因为皇帝刚一西征，来自北叙利亚的每年攻击——包括第一次越冬袭掠——就开始了，这绝非巧合。他是否真想像一份后来史料所报那样再次使罗马成为帝国都城，是一个有争议的问题。

他的目标似乎是击败伦巴第人并把他们纳入其统治，并重组阿非利加的防御与行政。他经塞萨洛尼基、雅典、科林斯与帕特雷进军，在帕特雷登船前往奥特朗托。他在意大利的战役不如计划成功，因为他未能夺取贝内文托（Beneventum），尽管商定了一项和约。他率军退到那不勒斯，然后访问罗马，参与了十二天的庆典与祈祷，受到教皇维塔利安（Vitalian）的欢迎（一志论似乎并未妨碍友好的接待）。此后他回到那不勒斯，再到西西里，在叙拉古设立总部。

Following the monothelete synod of 662, Constans set out on a major expedition to the west, a move that more likely reflects concerns connected with grain supplies and the other resources of Sicily and North Africa than a response to his apparent unpopularity. Constans likely viewed the western provinces as both strategically and politically key to imperial survival, for despite the Islamic naval challenge, the empire was still united by the Mediterranean. The risks were considerable, especially as far as Anatolia was concerned, for it is hardly a coincidence that as soon as the emperor had marched west the yearly attacks from North Syria, including the first overwintering raids, commenced. Whether he really wished to make Rome the capital of the empire once more as reported by a later source is a moot point.

His aim seems to have been to defeat the Lombards and incorporate them into his rule as well as to reor ga nize the defense and administration of Africa. He marched via Thessaloniki, Athens, Corinth, and Patras, where he embarked for Otranto. His campaign in Italy was less successful than planned, for he was unable to take Beneventum, although a peace treaty was agreed. Retiring with his forces to Naples, he then visited Rome and was involved in celebrations and prayer for twelve days, having been welcomed by Pope Vitalian (monotheletism does not appear to have hindered a friendly reception). Thereafter he returned to Naples and then to Sicily, where he established his headquarters at Syracuse.
无论他更长远的战略计划如何，鉴于他在岛上施加的负担，他的存在很快变得不得人心。财政困难迫使他向拉文纳教会借款，并从罗马夺取大量青铜与其他金属。作为对其支持的回报，拉文纳教座被授予自主权（autocephaly），这令教皇权十分恼怒。但他带着军队与朝廷的存在之不得人心，在史料中非常清楚：

Whatever his longer-term strategic plan, his presence on the island soon became unpopular, given the burdens it imposed. Financial difficulties forced him to borrow funds from the Church of Ravenna and to seize quantities of bronze and other metals from Rome. In return for its support, the see of Ravenna was granted autocephaly, much to the annoyance of the papacy. But the unpopularity of his presence, with his army and court, is very clear in the sources:
他在罗马停留十二天；他拆除了全城所有的青铜装饰；他取走了殉道者圣玛丽教堂（St Mary ad martyres）屋顶的青铜瓦，把它们送往帝都……他多年来以贡赋、人头税与船税，对卡拉布里亚、西西里、阿非利加与撒丁诸省的民众、居民与业主施加了前所未有的苦难，以致妻子甚至与丈夫分离、儿子与父母分离……他们从上帝的神圣教堂取走了所有圣器与设备，什么也没留下。

He stayed in Rome twelve days; he dismantled all the city’s bronze decorations; he removed the bronze tiles from the roof of the church of St Mary ad martyres, and sent them to the imperial city. . . He imposed such afflictions on the people, inhabitants and proprietors of the provinces of Calabria, Sicily, Africa and Sardinia for many years by tributes, poll-taxes and ship-money, such as had never been seen, so that wives were even separated from their husbands and sons from their parents. . . They took away all the sacred vessels and equipment from God’s holy churches, leaving nothing behind.
皇后与他们的三个儿子不被允许与他团聚，被国家高级官员与竞技党派（demes）成员扣留。最终，669年他成为一场暗杀阴谋的受害者，下手的是某位
寝宫侍从
（cubicularius）安德烈亚斯（Andreas），高级廷臣特罗伊卢斯（Troilus）之子；不久后亚美尼亚将军姆泽兹·格努尼（Mzez Gnouni），即米齐齐乌斯（Mizizius），很可能是帝国野战军奥普西基翁（Opsikion）的指挥官，被拥立为帝。

一种理论认为这场阴谋由穆阿维叶策划或至少支持；另一种认为它由君士坦丁堡宫廷的一群资深成员孵化，他们与某些亚美尼亚亲王热衷于与阿拉伯人的长期和平计划，其阴谋只是恰好与穆阿维叶在中、西地中海更富侵略性战略的发动同时；而第三种观点——也许最冷静、最可信——把这场阴谋看作君士坦丁堡高级指挥官与帝国精英成员对皇帝专注于意大利及巴尔干西北部事务，明知已有确切迹象表明阿拉伯人将大举进攻帝都，却迟迟未采取应对措施的回应。

The empress and their three sons were not permitted to join him, detained by senior officers of state and by members of the demes. Finally, in 669 he became the victim of an assassination plot at the hand of a certain
cubicularius,
Andreas, son of the senior courtier Troilus, and shortly thereafter the Armenian general Mzez Gnouni, or Mizizius, probably commander of the imperial field army, the Opsikion, was acclaimed emperor.

One theory has it that this plot was engineered or at least supported by Muʿāwiya; another that it was hatched by a group of senior members of the court in Constantinople who, along with certain Armenian princes, were keen on a long-term peace plan with the Arabs and whose plot merely coincided with the launch of Muʿāwiya’s more aggressive strategy in the central and western Mediterranean; while a third view, perhaps the most sober and plausible, sees the plot as a response on the part of the senior commanders and members of the imperial elite at Constantinople to the emperor’s inaction and preoccupation in Italy and in the northwest Balkan regions in the face of the clear evidence for the major Arab assault on the capital city of the empire.
无论哪种情况，君士坦斯被刺发生在最不利的时刻。穆阿维叶的指挥官们从陆路进攻北非罗马的比扎凯纳（Byzacena），从海路进攻沿海聚落与岛屿。亚美尼亚军区（Armeniakon）军队的指挥官、一个名叫萨博里乌斯（Saborius，即沙普尔Shapur）的亚美尼亚人，668年在穆阿维叶支持下反叛，意图与哈里发的军队会合进军君士坦丁堡；
尽管叛军首领猝逝结束了叛乱——该地区军队重新申明对帝国的忠诚——但这一事件典型地反映了政府在国家政策、地方认同与宗教问题之间复杂相互关系上不得不应对的困难。667/668年，很可能与所有这些发展相协调，穆阿维叶发动了对君士坦丁堡的第二次重大进攻，塞浦路斯、罗得岛、科斯岛与基齐库斯（Cyzicus）都被阿拉伯海军占领。
在西西里，米齐齐乌斯显然是不情愿地被拥立，而且似乎没什么支持。总督的军队得到来自阿非利加的部队增援，并可能在新皇帝君士坦丁四世本人率领一支海军到达后（在击败阿拉伯对君士坦丁堡的攻击之后），结束了这场篡夺，很可能在671或672年。叛乱的确切持续时间、以及姆泽兹之子约翰是否也发动了独立叛乱，仍悬而未决。不过不久后，阿拉伯人对西西里发动了另一次大规模袭掠，可能反映了君士坦斯治下驻扎那里的军队的撤离。

In either case, Constans’s assassination occurred at a most unfavorable moment. Muʿāwiya’s commanders launched attacks by land into Roman Byzacena in North Africa and by sea against coastal settlements and islands. The commander of the Armeniakon forces, an Armenian named Saborius (Shapur), rebelled with Muʿāwiya’s support in 668, intending to join forces with the caliph’s troops in their march on Constantinople;

and while the untimely death of the rebel ended the revolt— the troops of the region reaffirmed their loyalty to the empire— the event is symptomatic of the difficulties with which the government had to contend where the complex interrelationship between state policy, local identities, and religious questions were concerned. And in 667/668, probably coordinated with all these developments, Muʿāwiya launched a second major assault on Constantinople, with Cyprus, Rhodes, Cos, and Cyzicus all occupied by Arab naval forces.

In Sicily, Mizizius was apparently acclaimed against his will and in any case seems to have had little support. The forces of the exarch, reinforced by units from Africa and possibly with the arrival of a naval force under the new emperor, Constantine IV himself, after the defeat of the Arab attack on Constantinople, put an end to the usurpation, probably in 671 or 672. The exact length of the rebellion and whether or not Mzez’s son John also raised an independent revolt remain open. Shortly thereafter, though, the Arabs mounted another substantial raid on Sicily, possibly a reflection of the departure of the troops that had been based there under Constans.

很难评估君士坦斯的成就。他对哈里发国采取的是强硬的进攻政策，无疑基于局势终将在适当时候被扭转的假定。希拉克略通过顽强地坚持战争直到所需之时——就希拉克略而言，整整十八年——收复帝国失地、挫败敌人所树立的先例，不可能被忘记；的确，640年代参与君士坦斯政府的许多人必定直接参与了那场斗争，它在他们的集体记忆中还会相对新鲜。但君士坦斯通过在高加索扶植附庸与盟友来维持东部既定帝国国家的尝试并不成功，正如他通过移驻西西里来重新调整西部与北非帝国防御的努力也不成功。他及其顾问对帝国一志论的坚持——也许再次表明过于决心坚持希拉克略的政策目标——疏远了教皇权，并给皇帝在宫廷与自己核心家庭内部造成一些困难。他在"摄政"时期发行带"更新"主题的铜币、并在其亲政后延续，是他路径的一个标志——这一路径实际上拒绝承认已发生的任何戏剧性政治变化是永久的，而认为只需时间、耐心与努力就能逆转。他被认为创立了所谓的军区制度，但支持这一点的证据并不比支持皇帝希拉克略对此负责的旧主张的证据更多。他是否创建了一支拜占庭舰队（而非扩充和重组它），也仍是一个悬而未决的问题。

It is difficult to assess Constans’s achievement. His was a fiercely aggressive policy toward the caliphate, no doubt based upon the assumption that the situation could, in due course, be made good. The precedent set by Heraclius in recovering the empire’s lost territories and humbling its enemies by doggedly pursuing the war for as long as it took—in Heraclius’s case, a good eighteen years— cannot have been forgotten; indeed, many of those involved in Constans’s government in the 640s must have been directly involved in that struggle, and it would have been relatively fresh in their collective memory. But Constans’s attempts to maintain the established imperial state in the east through building up clients and allies in the Caucasus was not a success, no more than was his effort to reorient imperial defenses in the west and North Africa by his move to Sicily. His and his advisors’ adherence to imperial monotheletism— again perhaps indicating too much determination to adhere to the policy aims of Heraclius— alienated the papacy and caused the emperor some difficulties at court and within his own immediate family. The issue during his “regency” period of the copper coinage with the “renewal” motif and its continuation under his personal rule is an indication of his approach—an approach that in effect refused to recognize that any of the dramatic political changes that had occurred were permanent, but rather required merely time, patience, and effort to reverse. He has been attributed with the foundation of the so-called theme system, but there is no more evidence to support this than there is to support the older contention that the emperor Heraclius was responsible. Whether or not he created a Byzantine war fleet, as opposed to expanded and reorganized it, also remains an open question.
667–669年的封锁与围攻被击败，部分由于在海上部署了液体火这一新型恐怖武器，部分由于阿拉伯营地爆发的疾病。
此后，罗马人得以进行更多进攻性作战，674年在安纳托利亚击败阿拉伯纵队，同年也在海上击败他们。到677–678年，在叙利亚西北阿马努斯（Amanus）高地发生了涉及当地人与马尔代特人（Mardaites）的数月叛乱之后，
并面对不久后将爆发为内战（第二次
菲特纳
）的日益增长的内部反对，穆阿维叶不得不请求停止敌对行动。一项三十年和约被促成，附带每年支付三千金币、五十名拜占庭俘虏与五十匹种马。这对君士坦丁四世是一次显著的成功，立即重新确立了罗马的威望：阿瓦尔人的可汗与巴尔干各族的首领都承认帝国的宗主权。穆阿维叶死后哈里发国内部的纷争、以及680年叶齐德一世（Yazīd I）的即位，似乎为帝国提供了新机会，既在巩固方面，也在收复失地的希望方面。
The blockade and siege of 667–669 had been defeated partly by the deployment at sea of the new terror weapon of liquid fire and partly by disease that broke out in the Arab camp.

Thereafter, the Romans were able to conduct more offensive operations, defeating Arab columns in Anatolia in 674 and at sea in the same year. By 677–678, after several months of rebellion in the Amanus highlands of northwest Syria involving both locals and the Mardaites,
and faced by increasing internal opposition that would shortly thereafter break out into civil war (the second
fitna

), Muʿāwiya had to sue for a cessation of hostilities. A thirty-year peace was brokered, to be accompanied by a yearly payment of three thousand gold pieces, fifty Byzantine prisoners, and fifty stallions. This was a signal success for Constantine IV, immediately reestablishing Roman prestige: both the khagan of the Avars and the chieftains of the various Balkan peoples recognized imperial supremacy. Dissension within the caliphate after Muʿāwiya’s death and the accession of Yazīd I in 680 seemed to offer new opportunities to the empire, both in terms of consolidation as well as in respect of a hope for the recovery of lost provinces.
君士坦丁利用由此获得的喘息之机召集了一次普世会议，即第六次，680–681年在君士坦丁堡召开，教皇代表出席，会上帝国一志论被放弃、"正统"重新确立。

然而，要么在几个月前（更可能），要么在会议期间，皇帝离开去处理保加尔人到达多瑙河的问题。实际上这整个地区已不再处于帝国权威之下：有效控制仅限于希腊、伯罗奔尼撒与达尔马提亚的沿海聚落与堡垒。拜占庭堡垒与城镇频繁遭攻击，塞萨洛尼基尤其过着朝不保夕的生活，例如675–676年与677年再次被围。678–679年斯拉夫袭掠者从海路攻击帝国控制的岛屿；尽管660年代以后为重新申明帝国权威而进行的帝国远征影响非常有限，君士坦斯与君士坦丁四世都得以抓获大量俘虏并把他们运到安纳托利亚重新安置，以补偿阿拉伯袭掠活动造成的损失。
保加尔人的出现彻底改变了这一局面。

Constantine used the breathing space thus achieved to convoke an ecumenical council, the sixth, which was held at Constantinople in 680–681, at which papal representatives were present and at which imperial monotheletism was abandoned and “orthodoxy” reestablished.

Either a few months beforehand (more likely), or in the course of the council, however, the emperor left to deal with the arrival of the Bulgars on the Danube. In practical terms this whole region was no longer under imperial authority at all: effective control was restricted to coastal settlements and fortresses in Greece, the Peloponnese and Dalmatia. There were frequent attacks against Byzantine fortresses and towns, and Thessaloniki in particular led a precarious existence, besieged in 675–676 and again in 677, for example. Slav raiders attacked imperially-held islands by sea in 678–679; and while imperial expeditions undertaken to reassert imperial authority after the 660s had only a very limited impact, both Constans and Constantine IV were able to seize numbers of captives and transport them to Anatolia where they were resettled to compensate for the losses incurred through Arab raiding activity.
The appearance of the Bulgars changed this situation completely.

构成旧大保加利亚汗国的奥诺古尔—保加尔（Onogur-Bulgar）氏族联盟自希拉克略时代起就与帝国友好，并在罗马支持下摆脱了阿瓦尔人的统治。可萨人（Khazars）的到来导致这一群体崩溃，一些保加尔人加入可萨人，另一些西逃。其中一支在670年代到达多瑙河三角洲以北，希望定居在河以南的"罗马"土地并获取其肥沃牧场。皇帝不愿接纳他们，680年晚春，一旦东部前线的军队得以抽调，他便在一支舰队支持下进军讨伐。不幸的是，仅作战几个月后，君士坦丁就离开军队返回都城。原因仍不清楚：传统说法是他患痛风被迫撤退，使军队失去指挥。另一种更可信的解释是，他低估了一个已在多瑙河三角洲北部沼泽地占据稳固防御阵地的敌人，并假定他的军队可以安全地留下来处理一场比预期拖延更久的战役，而他不得不返回都城处理即将召开的普世会议的筹备。但在某个时候军队恐慌了，保加尔人得以击败帝国军队，在三角洲的沼泽与湿地立足。君士坦丁被迫迅速缔结一项条约，承认保加尔人对他们现在占据地区的占领，并额外同意每年纳贡。若干斯拉夫群体把名义上的效忠转给保加尔统治者，后者在普利斯卡（Pliska）建立都城——这一位置使保加尔人得以控制从多瑙河经安基亚卢斯（Anchialus）到君士坦丁堡的道路，以及通往多布罗加（Dobrudja）的通道。帝国现在第一次在巴尔干面对一个独立、有组织、潜在敌对的强权。

The confederation of Onogur-Bulgar clans that made up the khanate of old Great Bulgaria had had friendly relations with the empire since the time of Heraclius and had freed themselves from Avar domination with Roman support. The arrival of the Khazars resulted in the collapse of this grouping, with some Bulgars joining the Khazars and others fleeing west. One such group arrived north of the Danube delta during the 670s, hoping to settle on “Roman” land south of the river and gain access to its fertile pasture. Unwilling to admit them, the emperor marched against them, supported by a fleet, in the late spring of 680, once troops from the eastern front could be released. Unfortunately, and after only a few months of campaigning, Constantine left the army and returned to the capital. The reasons remain unclear: the traditional story is that he suffered from gout and was forced to withdraw, leaving the army without direction. The alternative, and more plausible, interpretation is that, underestimating an enemy that had occupied a secure defensive position in the marshlands of the northern delta of the Danube, and assuming his forces could safely be left to deal with a campaign that was dragging on longer than anticipated, he had to return to the capital to deal with the preparations for the upcoming ecumenical council. But at some point the troops panicked, and the Bulgars were able to defeat the imperial forces, establishing themselves in the marsh and fenlands of the delta. Constantine was forced quickly to conclude a treaty that recognized Bulgar occupation of the districts they now held and additionally agreed to an annual subsidy. A number of Slav groups transferred their nominal allegiance to the Bulgar ruler, who established a capital at Pliska— a location that permitted the Bulgars to control the road from the Danube via Anchialus to Constantinople as well as the approaches to the Dobrudja. The empire was now confronted for the first time with an independent, organized, and potentially hostile power in the Balkans.
680–681年会议的主要任务是撤销一能论与一志论，重新确立教会与政治的统一。毫无疑问，君士坦丁的主要目标是结束帝国相对的意识形态与政治孤立，尤其重新确立与教皇权的良好关系。付出的代价沉重：君士坦丁堡前牧首塞尔吉乌斯、皮鲁斯与保罗，连同亚历山大里亚的居鲁士与仍在世的安条克的马卡里乌斯（Macarius），以及教皇霍诺里乌斯一世——他们被共同认定负有责任——遭到谴责与绝罚。

共举行十八次会议，前十一次与最后一次会议由皇帝本人主持。尽管会议肯定反映了君士坦丁认识到由其父推动的教会分裂损害了他作为正统统治者与信仰捍卫者的地位、以及他在理论与神学意义上的权威，但宫廷与军队中肯定存在对这一改变的反对；的确，皇帝缺席第十二至十七次会议，可能直接与这些问题所需的复杂谈判、以及确定教会内部对皇帝新政策潜在支持或反对程度的需要有关。他的兄弟希拉克略与提比略被废黜与致残，似乎与士兵和高级指挥官的公开反对有关——也许也与最近出乎意料地败于保加尔人之手直接相关。抗议军队（显然来自安纳托利孔军（Anatolikon））的首领被逮捕处决。军队被送回基地。一志论继续有其拥护者——北叙利亚大部分地区似乎仍忠于它（见第2、3章），若干个人亦然，其中许多是军人。

The main task of the council of 680–681 was to revoke monoenergism and monotheletism and reestablish ecclesiastical and political unity. There can be no doubt that Constantine’s main aim was to end the empire’s relative ideological and political isolation and reestablish good relations with the papacy in particular. The price paid was heavy: the former patriarchs of Constantinople, Sergius, Pyrrhus, and Paul, along with Cyrus of Alexandria and the still living Macarius of Antioch, together with Pope Honorius I— who collectively were held responsible— were condemned and anathematized.

Eighteen sessions were held, presided over by the emperor himself for the first eleven and the during the final meeting. And while the council certainly reflects Constantine’s recognition that the split in the Church, promoted by his father, was injurious to his own position as orthodox ruler and defender of the faith and to his authority in theoretical and theological terms, there was certainly opposition at court and in the army to the change, indeed the emperor’s absence from sessions twelve to seventeen may be directly associated with the complex negotiations that these issues required and the need to determine the degree of potential support or opposition within the church for the emperor’s new policy. The deposition and mutilation of his brothers Heraclius and Tiberius seem to be connected with public opposition from both soldiers and senior commanders— perhaps also directly connected with the recent and unexpected defeat at the hands of the Bulgars. The leaders of the protesting troops (apparently from the Anatolikon division) were arrested and executed. The troops were returned to their bases. Monotheletism continued to have its adherents— much of northern Syria appears to have remained loyal to it (see Chapters 2 and 3), as did a number of individuals, many of them military.
尽管与罗马的和解也促成了与伦巴第人安排的和平，但它是以拉文纳教座的自治为代价实现的，因为683年君士坦丁再次把它置于罗马权威之下。

在阿非利加，尽管阿拉伯人成功袭掠深入罗马行省，总督区的关键堡垒与城市仍坚守，在君士坦丁最后几年里与土著部落结盟，对著名的阿拉伯领袖乌克巴（ʿUqba）取得重大胜利，后者的远征从利比亚五城地区发动，该地区自640年代起就在穆斯林手中。尽管有这类偶尔的成功，罗马军队很少能给阿拉伯人造成实质困难，大部分时间采取完全防御的姿态。随着土著柏柏尔氏族改宗伊斯兰，孤立的拜占庭聚落与设防中心相继陷落。迦太基697年被夺取，尽管698年短暂收复，同年晚些时候永久陷落。

While the reconciliation with Rome also facilitated a peace arranged with the Lombards, it was achieved at the cost of the autonomy of the see of Ravenna, since in 683 Constantine placed it once again under Roman authority.

In Africa, despite the successful Arab raids deep into the Roman provinces, key fortresses and cities in the exarchate held out, and during Constantine’s final years and in alliance with indigenous tribes a major victory was achieved over the renowned Arab leader ʿUqba, whose expeditions were launched from the Libyan Pentapolis, which had been in Muslim hands since the 640s. In spite of such occasional successes, the Roman forces contributed little to Arab difficulties, for the most part operating an entirely defensive posture. As the indigenous Berber clans were converted to Islam, so the isolated Byzantine settlements and fortified centers fell. Carthage was taken in 697 and, although briefly recovered in 698, fell permanently later in the same year.
此前盛行的相对稳定局面持续到683年，但君士坦丁利用那年因哈里发继承问题爆发的哈里发国内战，成功率军远征奇里乞亚，夺取莫普苏埃斯蒂亚（Mopsuestia），摧毁格尔马尼凯亚（Germanikeia）的阿拉伯堡垒并收复安条克，同时帝国舰队攻击了若干沿海城镇，包括阿什凯隆（Askalon）、凯撒利亚、阿卡（Acre）与推罗（Tyre）。连同马尔代特人的活动，这些行动迫使哈里发开启和平谈判。

正当阿拉伯领导层请求另一次休战时，君士坦丁于7月或9月去世，由其子查士丁尼二世继位，查士丁尼派将军莱昂提奥斯（Leontius）率军远征高加索，那里若干地区及其统治者暂时被带回早先对帝国的效忠。新哈里发阿卜杜勒·马利克（ʿAbd al-Malik）685年4月继承其父马尔万（Marwān），因此继承了一个极其危殆的局面，又因可萨人入侵高加索而加剧——他的亚美尼亚盟友在其中惨败，因此他急需与罗马人达成和解。穆阿维叶与君士坦丁四世缔结的条约被续签，因为它对查士丁尼极为有利：阿卜杜勒·马利克承诺每天支付一千
诺米斯玛
的贡赋，外加一匹象征性的马与一名奴隶，以换取拜占庭人停止推进。还商定分享塞浦路斯岛以及亚美尼亚与伊比利亚（Iberia）的收入。作为回报，马尔代特人——哈里发在北叙利亚的一大难题——被迁往小亚细亚西部。

The relatively stable situation that had prevailed lasted until 683, but, taking advantage of the civil war in the caliphate that had broken out in that year over the caliphal succession, Constantine led a successful expedition into Cilicia, taking Mopsuestia, destroying the Arab fortress at Germanikeia and recovering Antioch, while the imperial fleet attacked a number of coastal towns, including Askalon, Caesarea, Acre, and Tyre. Together with the activities of the Mardaites, these operations forced the caliph to open peace negotiations.

While the Arab leadership sued for another truce, Constantine died in either July or September and was succeeded by his son Justinian II, who launched an expedition under the general Leontius to the Caucasus, where a number of regions and their rulers were brought back for a while to their earlier allegiance with the empire. The new caliph, ʿAbd al-Malik, who succeeded his father, Marwān, in April 685, thus inherited an extremely precarious situation, exacerbated by a Khazar invasion of the Caucasus in which his Armenian allies were soundly defeated and urgently needed a settlement with the Romans. The treaty made by Muʿāwiya and Constantine IV was renewed, as it was extremely advantageously for Justinian: ʿAbd al-Malik undertook to pay a tribute of one thousand
nomismata

per day, together with a symbolic horse and a slave, in return for the Byzantines halting their advance. It was agreed also to share the income from the island of Cyprus as well as that from Armenia and Iberia. In return, the Mardaites, a major problem for the caliph in North Syria, were transferred to western Asia Minor.

随着东部前线压力减轻，查士丁尼得以把注意力转向巴尔干，687/688年他率军远征Sklaviniai（被各种斯拉夫与其他土著群体占据或控制的地区），推进到塞萨洛尼基，并在此过程中重新确立帝国在该地区的权威。然而他不得不一路打到马其顿，这一事实反映了实际现实。但他得以抓获大量俘虏并把他们迁往安纳托利亚，特别是比提尼亚与卡帕多西亚人口减少的地区，这些地区似乎受敌对力量存在之害最深。其中一些后来被编入行省军队，尽管许多随后逃亡。皇帝还把塞浦路斯部分人口迁往基齐库斯地区，该地区在阿拉伯封锁君士坦丁堡期间也受害严重，而马尔代特人被迁往伯罗奔尼撒与小亚细亚西南沿海地区。迁移俘虏以为遭受破坏的地区补充人口的政策本身并不新——例如查士丁尼一世与莫里斯（Maurice）统治期间就进行过这类迁移，这一政策在君士坦丁五世与巴西尔一世（Basil I）治下延续。查士丁尼也继续推行在高加索维持附庸公国的政策，689/690年亲自前往亚美尼亚强化其政策。但总体而言，帝国政策在高加索这方面的成败，取决于拜占庭对哈里发国的外交或军事行动总体上是否成功。罗马人一旦在战斗中被击败，该地区亚美尼亚与其他亲王往往就重新效忠哈里发国。

With pressure on the eastern front reduced, Justinian could turn his attention to the Balkans, and in 687/688 he led an expedition against the Sklaviniai, the regions occupied or controlled by various Slavic and other indigenous groups, pushing through to Thessaloniki and in the process reestablishing imperial authority in the region. The fact that he had to fight his way through to Macedonia reflects the practical realities, however. But he was able to take a large number of captives and transfer them to Anatolia, specifically to the depopulated regions of Bithynia and Cappadocia that appear to have suffered most from the presence of hostile forces. Some of these were later drafted into the provincial armies, although many subsequently deserted. The emperor also transferred part of the population of Cyprus to the Cyzicus region, also badly affected during the Arab blockade of Constantinople, while the Mardaites were moved to the Peloponnese and the southwest coastal region of Asia Minor. The policy of transferring captives to repopulate devastated areas was in itself not new— such transfers had been carried out during the reigns of Justinian I and Maurice, for example, and the policy was continued under Constantine V and Basil I. Justinian also continued to pursue a policy of maintaining client-principalities in the Caucasus and in 689/690 traveled to Armenia himself to reinforce his policies. But in general the success or failure of imperial policy in this regard in the Caucasus depended on the success or failure of Byzantine diplomatic or military action in respect of the caliphate more generally. As soon as the Romans were defeated in battle, the Armenian and other princes of the region tended to revert to their allegiance to the caliphate.
迁移塞浦路斯人是否违反与阿卜杜勒·马利克的协议，仍不清楚。
但692/693年休战被打破，在塞巴斯托波利斯（Sebastopolis）的一场大战中帝国军队被决定性击败，部分因为新征召的斯拉夫军队逃亡。次年罗马人的第二次推进被击退。后果是：第一，亚美尼亚亲王再次把效忠转给哈里发国，
而阿卜杜勒·马利克发动了对安纳托利亚新一轮定期袭掠，该地各行省刚刚开始从此前几十年的破坏中恢复。编年史家把这一切归因于查士丁尼对荣耀的渴望与其轻率的政治行动，在多大程度上正确，仍有争议。无论如何，东罗马国家再次陷入一场非常一边倒的冲突。九世纪初的编年史家狄奥凡尼斯报道，查士丁尼通过屠杀留在帝国境内的斯拉夫人来报复，尽管这一源自后来史料的记述的真实性可疑。逃亡者被安置在叙利亚。
Whether or not the transfer of the Cypriots was a breach of the agreement with ʿAbd al-Malik remains unclear.

But in 692/693 the truce was broken, and at a major battle at Sebastopolis the imperial forces were decisively defeated, partly because the recently conscripted Slav troops deserted. In the following year a second Roman thrust was thrown back. The consequence was, first, that the Armenian princes transferred their allegiance once more to the caliphate,

while ʿAbd al-Malik launched a new series of regular raids into Anatolia, the provinces of which had only just begun their recovery from the previous decades of devastation. To what extent the chroniclers were correct to attribute this to Justinian’s desire for glory and his rash political actions remains debated. In any case, the east Roman state was once again plunged into a very one-sided conflict. The early-ninth-century chronicler Theophanes reports that Justinian avenged himself by massacring the Slavs who remained within the empire, although the veracity of this account, derived from later sources, is dubious. The deserters were settled in Syria.
查士丁尼热衷于巩固其父的宗教政策，并巩固与教皇权的积极关系。687年他发表一份声明，由君士坦丁堡的教会与军队单位见证并确认，强调他接受680–681年第六次会议的结果，并强调他作为上帝代表与正统信仰选定守护者的职能。他把格言
基督的仆人
（servus Christi）连同基督半身像铸在钱币上，强调其权威的神圣来源。然而，阿卜杜勒·马利克改革后的币制是对此的回应、或查士丁尼改革后的
诺米斯玛
是对阿卜杜勒·马利克币制的回应，似乎不太可能，尽管我们不应绝对否认其中涉及的宣传战要素，即便它很可能是附带的，因为这种紧张随后发展为两位统治者之间条约的破裂，并导致693年塞巴斯托波利斯之战与罗马人的失败。

Justinian was keen to consolidate the religious policies of his father and to cement a positive relationship with the papacy. In 687 he issued a statement, witnessed and confirmed by the Church and the army units at Constantinople, underlining his acceptance of the results of the sixth council of 680–681 and stressing his function as God’s representative and chosen guardian of orthodoxy. In placing the motto
servus Christi
on his coins, together with a bust of Christ, he stressed the divine source of his authority. That ʿAbd al-Malik’s reformed coinage was a response to this or Justinian’s reformed
nomisma

was a response to ʿAbd al-Malik’s coinage seems unlikely, however, although we should not deny absolutely the element of propaganda warfare involved, even if it may well have been incidental, for this tension then developed into a breach of the treaty between the two rulers and led to the battle at Sebastopolis and the Roman defeat in 693.

但在691/692年，为确认其意识形态纲领，查士丁尼召集了所谓的五六会议（Quinisext）或特鲁洛会议（Trullan Council）——之所以如此称呼，是因为它确认了553年与680–681年第五、第六次普世会议所处理的事项——并在皇宫的特鲁洛斯（Trullos，即圆顶大厅）召开。有人主张，这正是查士丁尼改革币制所针对的语境——一个特定的罗马语境，其中帝国币制可被理解为通过图像手段强化并进一步增加会议决议的权威。
若干关于教士纪律的"西方"传统被拒绝，而第82条教规禁止把基督表现为羔羊——这在西方日益普遍——坚持他应以人的形象呈现；第36条教规（继381年君士坦丁堡会议第3条与451年卡尔西顿会议第28条之后）强调罗马与君士坦丁堡教座在优先于耶路撒冷、安条克与亚历山大里亚教座方面的平等地位。

But in the year 691/692, in confirmation of his ideological program, Justinian had convoked the so-called Quinisext or Trullan Council (so-called because it confirmed the matters treated at the fifth and sixth ecumenical councils, in 553 and 680–681) and met in the Trullos or domed hall of the imperial palace. And this was the context, it has been argued, for which Justinian’s reformed coinage was devised— a specifically Roman context, in which the imperial coinage could be understood to reinforce and further add authority through iconographic means to the decisions of the council.

A number of “Western” traditions in respect of clerical discipline were rejected, while canon 82 prohibited the representation of Christ as a lamb— increasingly common in the West— insisting that he be presented in human form, while canon 36 (following canon 3 of the council of Constantinople of 381 and canon 28 of the council of Chalcedon of 451) emphasized the parity of the sees of Rome and Constantinople in their precedence over the sees of Jerusalem, Antioch, and Alexandria.
当然，教皇的反对使君士坦丁堡与罗马再次冲突。教皇权挑战会议的普世有效性，查士丁尼遵循帝国先例，下令逮捕教皇。罗马与拉文纳的军队都反对此举，被委派此任务的
首席持剑侍卫
（prōtospatharios）扎卡里亚斯（Zacharias）求得教皇庇护才免遭武力袭击。但皇帝的财政政策已使他在君士坦丁堡与行省都深不得人心。他似乎激起了统治集团、尤其元老院的重大反对。695年他在一场政变中被推翻，过程中最近被任命指挥希腊（Hellas）军事力量的将军莱昂提奥斯被拥立为帝。在元老院要员与宫廷军队的支持下，查士丁尼及其可恨的下属被抓获。皇帝被割裂鼻子与舌头，流放赫尔松。

Papal opposition brought Constantinople and Rome once more into conflict, of course. The papacy challenged the ecumenical validity of the council, and Justinian, following imperial precedent, ordered the pope’s arrest. The troops in both Rome and Ravenna were opposed to this, and the
prōtospatharios

Zacharias, who had been delegated with this task, escaped violence only by throwing himself on the pope’s mercy. But the emperor’s fiscal policies had already made him deeply unpopular both at Constantinople and in the provinces. He seems to have aroused substantial opposition in the leading circles and the senate in particular. In 695 he was overthrown in a coup, in the course of which the general Leontius, recently appointed to command the military forces in Hellas, was acclaimed emperor. With support from leading members of the senate and the palatine troops, Justinian and his hated subordinates were seized. The emperor had his nose and tongue slit and was banished to Cherson.
莱昂提奥斯似乎是个受欢迎的人选，但只做了三年皇帝。第二年他面对高加索拉齐卡的一场叛乱，同样是在他统治期间，东罗马在阿非利加的权力最终被扑灭。迦太基697年陷落于阿拉伯攻击，莱昂提奥斯接到消息后派遣舰队与军队去收复。他们成功了，但强大的阿拉伯反攻迫使他们撤退。这是总督区在阿非利加的最后一个前哨，它的丧失意味着罗马北非的终结。
舰队在指挥官约翰（John）率领下撤到克里特等待命令，但士兵哗变，拥立他们自己的指挥官、
营长
（drouggarios）阿普西马尔（Apsimar）为帝。军队驶向君士坦丁堡，在金角湾的叙凯（Sykai）港登陆并围攻该城，该城当时正遭受瘟疫流行，但仍坚守了约六个月，直到部分守军打开城门。莱昂提奥斯被致残以丧失帝位资格，被囚禁在君士坦丁堡的一座修道院。阿普西马尔采用帝名提比略，从而把自己与希拉克略家族联系起来并使其统治正当化。

Leontius, who appears to have been a popular choice, was emperor for a mere three years. In his second year he was faced with a rebellion in Lazica in the Caucasus, and it was likewise during his reign that east Roman power in Africa was finally extinguished. Carthage fell to an Arab attack in 697, upon receiving news of which Leontius dispatched a fleet and troops to retake it. They were successful, but a strong Arab counterattack forced their withdrawal. This was the last outpost of the exarchate in Africa, and its loss meant an end to Roman North Africa.
The fleet, under its commander, John, withdrew to Crete to await orders, but the soldiers mutinied and proclaimed as emperor their own commander, the
drouggarios

Apsimar. Sailing to Constantinople, the army landed at the port of Sykai on the Golden Horn and besieged the city, which was suffering from a plague epidemic at the time, yet held out for some six months until some of the garrison opened the gates. Leontius was mutilated to disqualify him from the imperial throne and confined to a monastery in Constantinople. Apsimar adopted the imperial name of Tiberius, thus associating himself with the family of Heraclius and legitimating his rule.
提比略·阿普西马尔（一般如此称呼）在位到705年。在他统治期间，阿拉伯人在安纳托利亚的入侵与袭掠步伐加快，前线被逐步向北、向西推。北非完全得不到关注，所有努力都集中在安纳托利亚。这里皇帝的兄弟希拉克略指挥行省骑兵，得以取得适度成功，尽管这并未影响根本的战略局势。亚美尼亚高地亲王与统治者的反复无常肯定影响了帝国战略与帝国保卫其核心地区的能力。
纳哈拉尔
（nakharars，亚美尼亚贵族）703年接受穆斯林权威后，次年再次反叛并号召罗马人支持他们的战斗。

有一些证据表明南巴尔干有军事行动；查士丁尼二世治下迁往基齐库斯地区的一些塞浦路斯人返回了塞浦路斯。提比略还修缮了君士坦丁堡的海防，这些海防此前被任其衰败、有些地方已坍塌。然而他只统治了七年，因为705年查士丁尼在保加尔可汗特尔维尔（Tervel）帮助下得以返回。在一支保加尔军队支持下，他得以通过一条高架渠进入城内，并在其支持者帮助下迅速夺取控制权。莱昂提奥斯与提比略·阿普西马尔都被处决，查士丁尼加冕其子提比略为共帝。

Tiberius Apsimar, as he is generally known, held the throne until 705. During his reign the pace of Arab incursions and raids in Anatolia increased and the frontier was progressively pushed north and west. North Africa received no attention at all, all efforts being concentrated on Anatolia. Here the emperor’s brother Heraclius commanded the provincial cavalry forces and was able to achieve moderate success, although this did not affect the fundamental strategic situation. The fickleness of the princes and rulers of the Armenian highlands certainly affected imperial strategy and the ability of the empire to defend its core regions. Having accepted Muslim authority in 703, the
nakharars
rebelled once again the following year and called on Roman support in their fight.

There is some evidence of military action in the southern Balkans; and some of the Cypriots who had removed to the Cyzicus region under Justinian II returned to Cyprus. Tiberius also carried out repairs to the sea defenses of Constantinople, which had been allowed to decay and in places collapse. He reigned only seven years, however, for in 705 Justinian was able to return with the help of the Bulgar khan Tervel. Supported by a Bulgar force, he was able to gain access through one of the viaducts into the city and with the help of his supporters there was quickly able to seize control. Leontius and Tiberius Apsimar were both executed, and Justinian had his son Tiberius crowned co emperor.

特尔维尔被授予凯撒头衔，查士丁尼随后着手搜捕并处决或以其他方式惩罚那些反对过他的人，然后开始了一场报复性的恐怖统治。他似乎尤其热衷于恢复与教皇权的友好关系。夺回皇位后不久，两位都主教被派往罗马，携带帝国书信，皇帝在信中提议召集一次普世会议，会上他将确认教皇希望的691/692年会议的任何教规。无论原因如何，教皇约翰七世（John VII）拒绝行动，只是把主教们与帝国圣旨（sacra）退回给皇帝——鉴于查士丁尼提出的重大让步，这是一个令人惊讶的回应，连
《教皇名录》
（Liber pontificalis）中约翰传记条目的作者都觉得难以理解。
然而查士丁尼没有放弃，710年邀请教皇（当时是君士坦丁一世，Constantine I）访问君士坦丁堡。教皇在都城受到年轻皇帝提比略在元老院陪同下接待，然后前往尼科米底亚，在那里他会见皇帝，皇帝向他行
俯伏礼
（proskynēsis）。罗马教座的特权得到确认，就五六会议中在罗马引起冒犯的各条教规达成一致，商定了一项不成文协议，教皇于711年秋返回罗马。
然而在筹备君士坦丁访问期间，查士丁尼不得不处理拉文纳的一场叛乱，叛军反对教廷，也反对君士坦丁四世取消拉文纳相对于罗马教座的自治权。一支海军被派去处理此事，尽管在后来的传统中，这次远征被归因于查士丁尼对拉文纳支持695年废黜他的严厉报复。

Tervel was granted the title of Caesar, and Justinian then proceeded to hunt down and have those who had opposed him executed or otherwise punished before embarking on a vengeful reign of terror. He seems to have been especially keen to restore friendly relations with the papacy. Soon after his recovery of the throne, two metropolitan bishops were sent to Rome with imperial letters in which the emperor offered to convene an ecumenical council at which he would confirm whichever of the canons of the council of 691/692 the pope wished. Whatever the reason, Pope John VII refused to act and simply returned the bishops and the imperial sacra to the emperor, a surprising response given the substantial concessions offered by Justinian— even the author of John’s biographical notice in the
Liber pontificalis
found this difficult to understand.

Justinian did not give up, however, and in 710 invited the pope, by then Constantine I, to visit Constantinople. The pope was received in the capital by the young emperor Tiberius accompanied by the senate, before proceeding to Nikomedeia, where he met with the emperor, who performed
proskynēsis

before him. The privileges of the Roman see were confirmed, agreement was reached on the various canons of the Quinisext that had caused offense in Rome, an unwritten accord was agreed, and the pope returned to Rome in the fall of 711.

In the course of the preparations for Constantine’s visit, however, Justinian had to deal with a rebellion in Ravenna which was hostile to the papacy and the fact that Constantine IV had rescinded its autonomy vis- à- vis Rome. A naval force was sent to deal with this, although in later tradition the expedition was ascribed to Justinian’s exacting revenge for Ravennate support for his deposition in 695.

然而查士丁尼确实派遣了一支惩罚性远征军去赫尔松，表面上是为了在该地区重新确立帝国权威以对抗可萨人的蚕食。该城再次反叛查士丁尼后，第二支远征军被派出。在随后的混乱中舰队哗变，拥立一位被流放的军官巴尔达内斯（Bardanes）为帝，并驶向君士坦丁堡。查士丁尼离开去奥普西基翁与亚美尼亚军区征召军队，但他的盟友抛弃他、任其命运摆布。巴尔达内斯采用帝名菲利皮科斯（Philippicus），搜出查士丁尼及其子，两人都被杀。查士丁尼之死终结了希拉克略王朝，随之而来的是一个政治不稳定时期。执事阿加通（Agathon）是这些事件的目击者，他把它描述为帝国权威被蔑视、帝国被屈辱的时期。暴政、篡夺与权力的暴力更迭是这一时期的特征。为试图恢复帝国权威、唤起过去的胜利与成功、并巩固自己的地位，新皇帝颁布一道敕令，谴责680–681年第六次普世会议的决议，重新确立一志论为官方信经。正如狄奥凡尼斯所说："菲利皮科斯不以猛烈攻击神圣的第六次普世会议为耻，急于颠覆由它确认的神圣教义。"

Justinian did send a punitive expedition to Cherson, however, ostensibly to reestablish imperial authority in the region against Khazar encroachment. After another revolt against Justinian in the city, a second expedition was dispatched. In the ensuing confusion the fleet mutinied; proclaimed an exiled officer, Bardanes, emperor; and sailed to Constantinople. Justinian left to raise troops in the Opsikion and Armeniakon regions, but his allies abandoned him to his fate. Bardanes, who had adopted the imperial name Philippicus, sought Justinian and his son out and both were killed. Justinian’s death ended the dynasty of Heraclius, and a period of political instability followed. The deacon Agathon, an eyewitness of the events, described it as a time during which imperial authority was treated with contempt and the empire was humbled. Tyranny, usurpation, and violent changes of power characterized the period. In an attempt to restore imperial authority, to recall past victories and successes, and to consolidate his own position, the new emperor issued an edict condemning the acts of the sixth ecumenical council of 680–681 and reestablishing monotheletism as the official creed. As Theophanes put it, “Philippicus was not ashamed to make a furious attack on the holy sixth ecumenical council, hastening to subvert the divine doctrines that had been confirmed by it.”
这一举动有多少支持仍不清楚——教士似乎大体接受了它（包括后来的牧首格尔马努斯Germanus以及讲道者克里特的安德烈Andrew of Crete），尽管证据稀少，而对帝国报复的恐惧会抑制公开反对。来自罗马的反对不可避免，教皇权退回了菲利皮科斯的肖像——按惯例由新皇帝送往罗马——连同他的一志论正统声明。

How much support this move had remains unclear— the clergy seem largely to have accepted it (including the later patriarch Germanus as well as the homilist Andrew of Crete), although the evidence is sparse and fear of imperial reprisals would have discouraged open opposition. Opposition from Rome was inevitable and the papacy returned Philippicus’s portrait, sent to Rome by the new emperor, as was the custom, along with his monothelete declaration of orthodoxy.

我们应当记得，在这场内部政治动荡之中，帝国边境沿线的敌对活动持续不减。在巴尔干，查士丁尼与可汗特尔维尔达成协议后盛行相对和平的局面，但那位皇帝被废黜给了特尔维尔入侵的借口，他的军队蹂躏了色雷斯南部直到君士坦丁堡城墙。阿拉伯人对安纳托利亚的袭掠每年继续，罗马防御继续失地。堡垒城镇提亚纳（Tyana）707/708年在罗马援军被击败后陷落；边境城镇西锡翁（Sision）711年被放弃；阿马塞亚（Amaseia）、米斯提亚（Misthia）与皮西迪亚的安条克712–713年被劫掠；罗马军队不得不放弃梅利泰内（Melitene）周围一系列设防据点。
菲利皮科斯着手准备反击这些袭掠，但713年初夏奥普西基翁军区的士兵哗变。皇帝6月被废黜并致盲，
首席秘书
（prōtoasēkrētis）阿尔忒弥奥斯（Artemius），一位宫廷文书官，成为皇帝阿纳斯塔修斯二世。

We should recall that, in the midst of this internal political turmoil, hostile activity along the empire’s frontiers continued unabated. In the Balkans there prevailed a relatively peaceful situation following Justinian’s agreement with Khan Tervel, but that emperor’s deposition gave Tervel an excuse to invade, and his forces devastated southern Thrace as far as the walls of Constantinople. Arab raids on Anatolia continued on an annual basis, and the Roman defenses continued to lose ground. The fortress town of Tyana fell in 707/708 after a Roman relief force was defeated; the frontier town of Sision was abandoned in 711; Amaseia, Misthia, and Antioch in Pisidia were sacked in 712–713; and Roman forces had to abandon a series of fortified strongholds around Melitene.
Philippicus undertook preparations to counter these raids, but in early summer 713 the soldiers of the Opsikion division mutinied. The emperor was deposed and blinded in June, and the
prōtoasēkrētis
Artemius, a palatine clerical official, became emperor as Anastasius II.
阿纳斯塔修斯的第一步是恢复卡尔西顿正统并为第六次会议平反。面对即将到来的攻击，加强君士坦丁堡防御的措施被启动。一支海军被装备起来，试图通过攻击港口中的阿拉伯船只来先发制人地阻止对该城的封锁。

但奥普西基翁军队再次哗变，这次是在罗得岛，远征军正在那里集结。他们返回大陆，与其他部队一起拥立一位此前默默无闻的财政官员狄奥多西（Theodosius）为帝。尽管他试图回避这一可疑的荣誉，他被阻止离开，被迫接受军队的拥立。叛乱部队进军君士坦丁堡，该城在短暂围攻后投降。阿纳斯塔修斯已离开该城、避难尼西亚，不过在此之前他通过入侵军队的指挥官马斯拉马（Maslama）向哈里发发出呼吁，请求军事援助以对抗篡位者。
但他很快退位，作为修士隐退塞萨洛尼基。
